fields.features_heading: What Goes Into an IT Survey Built With Emergent
fields.features_subheading: Name the IT areas staff should rate and who hears about a low score. Emergent builds each piece below from that prompt.
fields.feature_1:
Questions for each part of IT

Tell Emergent which parts of IT to rate, such as the help desk or the apps staff use. Emergent drafts questions for each part, and a follow-up prompt changes any of them.
fields.feature_2:
Every answer in a database you own

Each answer is saved as a row in a database you own, tagged with the department and the ticket number. Put this spring's support score beside last spring's before the budget review.
fields.feature_3:
Low ratings emailed to the help desk lead

A low score reaches the help desk lead by email, with the ticket number and the comment attached. You pick the score that sends it, and a Slack or in-app alert works too.
fields.feature_4:
One question per screen on a phone

Employees answer on a phone, one question per screen, from a warehouse floor or a classroom. Keep the check to 3 questions, and a new hire finishes it between orientation sessions.
fields.feature_5:
Ticket data from your help desk

Ticket data comes in from your help desk through its API, so each survey goes out with the ticket number and category filled in. Ratings can sync back to that same tool.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and the full code

On paid plans, the full code exports to your GitHub repository and stays with your IT team. Host the survey on your own domain, included in Emergent and billed in credits.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four IT Teams Put Their Surveys to Work
fields.tab_content_1:
9 of 14 low ratings came from VPN tickets

Brennock Freight's IT team asks for a rating from 1 to 5 and a comment each time a ticket closes. In September, 214 of 530 closed tickets got a rating. The help desk lead gets an email for any 1 or 2, and 9 of the 14 low ratings came from VPN tickets. The team rewrote its VPN setup guide that week.
fields.tab_content_2:
The visualization team rates IT 2.1 out of 5

Every spring, Quillmont Architects asks its staff to rate IT support from 1 to 5, and this year 118 of 140 answered. Five departments scored IT 3.9 or higher. The visualization team gave it 2.1, and its comments describe renders that run overnight on old workstations. IT moved that team's workstation refresh up to January.
fields.tab_content_3:
Diagram app seats cut to 25 after 17 showed weekly use

Fenwick Hollow School District pays for 5 licensed apps by the seat. Before renewal, it asks staff which ones they open each week, and 231 of 260 answered. The diagram app has 120 seats and 17 weekly users. The district renewed 25 seats instead of 120.
fields.tab_content_4:
Laptop setup starts 5 days early, and 19 of 22 are ready

New hires at Saltmarsh Bakery Co. get a short IT check on their phone on day 3, one question per screen. It opens with one question: was your laptop ready on your first morning? In spring, 11 of 21 said yes. IT then began each laptop setup 5 days before the start date, and in summer 19 of 22 said yes.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an IT Survey
fields.howto_description: Follow these 7 steps to plan an IT survey and turn its lowest score into a fix your IT team can schedule.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Choose the moment it goes out
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Add one open question per rating
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the one decision the results should settle, such as which app seats to renew or which team gets new workstations first. Put it in the first line of your prompt to Emergent. Cut any question whose answer could not change that decision.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Match the send time to the survey. A ticket survey goes out when the ticket closes, while the fix is fresh. A company-wide support rating fits once a year, a few weeks before the IT budget is set. A new hire check fits the first week.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write the rating question first and keep its scale fixed, such as 1 to 5 on how well IT solved the problem. With the same scale every round, this year's score sits beside last year's and the change means something.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Under each rating, ask one open question: what would have made this better? A low score shows where IT falls short. The comment beside it names the laptop or the app behind that score, and that is the part your team can fix.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Save the department, site, or ticket category with each answer, and leave names out unless someone will follow up. That one field turns a single company score into a list of teams you can sort, lowest first, before you plan the fixes.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Name one person, such as the help desk lead, and the score that alerts them. Before launch, test the survey with 5 sample answers, including one that should trigger the alert, and confirm the email arrives with the ticket number.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Within a month of closing the survey, tell staff what changed because of their answers. One line in the next company email is enough, such as a rewritten VPN guide. People answer the next round when the last one led somewhere.

faq_plan.a: An IT survey asks employees how well IT support and their work tools serve them. It can rate a single help desk ticket or a full year of support, and the scores show the IT team which fix matters most to staff.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an IT survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI survey builder in one prompt: what staff will rate and who gets an email when a score is low. Emergent builds the survey, its logic, and the database behind it. Change any question by prompting again before the first round goes out.

faq_plan.q: What IT survey questions should I ask employees about help desk support?
faq_plan.a: Ask about the last ticket, not IT in general. How well was your problem solved, on a scale of 1 to 5? How long did you wait for a first reply? Did you have to explain the problem more than once? What one thing would have made it better? Keep the help desk set to 4 questions.

faq_plan.q: What should an IT survey template include?
faq_plan.a: Include a fixed rating scale, one open comment box under each rating, and a field for the department or ticket category. Add a plain yes or no item for facts, such as whether a laptop was ready on time; a yes no questions survey shows how to word those. Stop at 8 questions.

faq_plan.q: What are some IT survey examples beyond the help desk?
faq_plan.a: A device survey asks whether each laptop keeps up with the work. A remote work survey asks about home internet and the VPN. A security survey checks whether staff know how to report a suspicious email, and a training survey asks which tools people want help with. Any of them can go to every employee, since Emergent puts no cap on responses.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should an IT survey have?
faq_plan.hint: How does gallup develop questions for its surveys?
faq_plan.a: Keep a ticket survey to 2 questions, a rating and a comment, since it arrives after every fix. A yearly IT survey can run 10 to 15 questions across 4 or 5 areas. Past 15, cut any question whose answer cannot change a decision.

faq_plan.q: How do I get more employees to answer an IT survey?
faq_plan.a: Keep it short, send it from the IT lead by name, and say in the invite which decision the answers feed. Emergent can build it as one question per screen, which staff can answer on a phone between tasks. Keep the tone plain: playful lines belong in a set of funny survey questions for a team event.

faq_plan.q: Should an IT survey be anonymous?
faq_plan.a: Yes for the yearly survey, and no for ticket surveys. Save only the department with yearly answers, and staff rate support more frankly. A ticket survey carries the ticket number, which lets the help desk follow up on a 1 or 2. Say in the invite which kind staff are answering.

faq_plan.q: How often should I run an IT survey across the company?
faq_plan.a: Once a year, timed to land before next year's IT spending is planned. Between rounds, send a short pulse after a big change, such as a new laptop rollout or an email migration. Each round saves to a database you own, where last year's scores sit beside this year's.

faq_plan.q: Should IT send a survey after every closed help desk ticket?
faq_plan.a: Yes, send one after every closed ticket. Keep it to a rating plus one comment box. It works like a post purchase survey: short, sent right after the event, and about that one experience. If one person has several tickets closed in a week, send them a single survey.

plan.angle: IT survey searches want question lists for rating internal IT support: help desk tickets, devices, software and onboarding. Template pages list questions and stop. This page shows four IT surveys that each end in a decision an IT team makes: a freight company's help desk tracing low ratings to VPN tickets, an architecture firm finding the one department that rates IT poorly, a school district cutting unused app seats before renewal, and a bakery chain fixing new-hire laptop setup. The FAQ covers questions, templates, examples, length, response rates, anonymity, cadence and per-ticket surveys as plain advice.
tab_stories: Brennock Freight's IT team asks two questions when a ticket closes; in September 214 of 530 closed tickets got a rating, 14 were a 1 or 2, and 9 of those 14 were VPN tickets, each one emailed to the help desk lead.

Quillmont Architects asks all 140 staff to rate IT support from 1 to 5 each spring; 118 answer, 5 departments score 3.9 or higher, and the visualization team scores 2.1, with comments about renders that run overnight on old workstations.

Before license renewal, Fenwick Hollow School District asks its staff which of 5 licensed apps they open each week; 231 of 260 answer, and the diagram app shows 17 weekly users on 120 seats, so the district renews 25.

Saltmarsh Bakery Co. asks each new hire on day 3, one question per screen on a phone, whether the laptop was ready on the first morning; in the second quarter 11 of 21 said yes, and after IT began setup 5 days before each start date, 19 of 22 said yes in the third.
